title: Landing hero ops-econ compact playbook
audience: Primary: engineering and platform leads evaluating inference for product features; Secondary: startup founders and infra/platform teams at mid-market enterprise companies.
primary_headline_variants: Ship predictable LLM performance — without owning the stack
Inference that hits latency targets and unit-cost goals
Keep output quality high while cutting per-token spend
The inference runtime your product teams can rely on
subhead_variants: Unified API for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — built for production economics and SLAs
Lower latency, predictable costs, and fallbacks that keep features online
From early experiments to mission-critical rollouts: consistent inference behavior across environments
supporting_bullets: Run on hosted endpoints or reserve dedicated capacity with SLA-backed latency
Automatic batching, prefix caching, and model quantization guidance to reduce unit costs
Smart routing and automatic fallback to maintain availability during spikes
hero_visual_direction: A minimal illustration showing three environments (cloud API, dedicated GPU pool, VPC box) connected by a single API layer; small overlays indicate latency graph and cost-savings badge. Tone: technical, tidy, not flashy.
key_objections: We can self-host cheaper — rebuttal: total cost of ownership for production latency and ops is higher; show TCO example
Vendor lock-in concerns — rebuttal: consistent API and private deployment options with exportable configurations
Quality regressions from quantization/optimizations — rebuttal: Redwood Optimize and eval hooks tied to prompt sets
competitive_hooks: Explicit unit-economics play: show per-1000-token cost examples with/without batching
SLA and fallbacks: highlight automated model variant routing and regional failover
Developer ergonomics: one API surface across hosted/dedicated/private, clear SDK examples and quickstart
success_metrics: Homepage hero CTR to signup: baseline 2.2% -> target 3.5% in 4 weeks
Benchmark page visits from hero secondary CTA: +25%
Qualified demo requests for Dedicated from hero flows: 12 leads/month
experiment_plan: A/B test 4-week run. Variant A: headline 1 + CTA 'Get started — free credits'. Variant B: headline 3 + CTA 'Benchmark your model now'. Track signup conversion, time-to-first-call, and benchmark-run completion rate. Segment by company size and initial latency budget.
notes_to_copy: Draft is intentionally compact — target engineers who skim. Leave room for a one-line trust band (logos) under the hero. Questions: should we surface 'SLA-backed' in the primary subhead or save for a secondary line? Need benchmark GIF from performance team (INFR-3019). Keep tone pragmatic, avoid buzzwords like 'revolutionary'.
